title: Writing System and User Prompts
group: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55-60%)

Create effective system and user prompts for generative AI models
the official AI-901 study guide, skills measured as of April 15, 2026

toc.title: What goes in a system prompt

html:
1Message roles

A request to a chat model is a list of messages. Each message has a role.

Role Who writes it Purpose
System The developer Sets the role, rules, tone and limits of the assistant for the whole conversation
User The person using the app The question or task for this turn
Assistant The model The reply; earlier replies are sent back as context

The system message is optional, but include at least a basic one for the best results. In some APIs the system message is passed as instructions. Beyond the study guide

Exam tip

. System prompt = standing rules from the developer ("You are a polite support assistant for Fabrikam; answer only about our products"). User prompt = the question of the moment.

2What goes in a system prompt

Element Example
Role "You are a travel assistant for Fabrikam Outdoors."
Scope "Answer only questions about camping gear and our store."
Tone and style "Be friendly and concise. Use plain English."
Format "Reply with three bullet points." or "Return valid JSON."
Rules and safety "If you do not know, say so. Never share personal data."
Examples One or two sample question and answer pairs

3Writing an effective user prompt

Technique Why it helps Weak vs better
Be clear and specific Less guessing "Tell me about tents" → "List three features to compare when choosing a four-person tent."
Give context The model only knows what is in the prompt Add the audience, goal and data
State the format Easier to use the output "Answer as a table with two columns."
Give examples (few-shot) Shows the pattern Add sample input and output pairs
Break a big task into steps More reliable "First list the issues, then rank them."
Set the length Avoids rambling "In under 50 words."
Provide the source text Grounds the answer "Using only the text below…"

Zero-shot means no examples; one-shot and few-shot give one or several examples. Few-shot examples are sent as user and assistant messages. Few-shot tricks are not recommended for reasoning models. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Developer rules go in the system prompt; the person's question goes in the user prompt.

4The model has no memory

The model does not remember earlier calls. For a conversation, the app sends the earlier messages again with each request, within the context window. Long chats cost more tokens.

5Safety and reliability in prompts

  • Tell the model what to do when it lacks information ("If the answer is not in the text, say 'I don't know'"). This reduces made-up answers.
  • Ground the answer in trusted text you provide.
  • Never put secrets or personal data in a prompt unless needed and permitted.
  • A user can try to override your rules with a prompt ("ignore the previous instructions"). This is prompt injection; keep rules in the system message and add platform safety settings. Beyond the study guide
Exam tip

. To make the model stay in a role and on topic → use the system prompt. To make output consistent in format → state the format and give examples. To make answers factual from your data → provide the data in the prompt.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants its chatbot always to answer politely and only about camping gear. Where should this rule go?

  • AIn every user message
  • BIn the model name
  • CIn the deployment region
  • DIn the system prompt
Show the answer

Answer: D. The system prompt sets the standing role, scope and tone for the conversation.

S2A team wants every answer returned as valid JSON with the same fields. Which approach helps most?

  • AAsk the model to be creative with the layout
  • BRaise the temperature and hope for the same layout
  • CState the exact format and give an example in the prompt
  • DRemove the system message to simplify the request
Show the answer

Answer: C. A clear format instruction with an example makes the output consistent.

S3A prompt that contains two sample question and answer pairs before the real question is called what?

  • AZero-shot
  • BA system image
  • CA token limit
  • DFew-shot
Show the answer

Answer: D. Giving several examples in the prompt is few-shot prompting.

S4A user asks about a policy that is not in the provided text. How should the system prompt tell the model to behave to reduce made-up answers?

  • AAlways guess an answer that sounds plausible
  • BUse a higher temperature so answers sound confident
  • CSay that it does not know when the answer is not in the text
  • DIgnore the provided text and use general knowledge
Show the answer

Answer: C. Telling the model to admit when information is missing reduces hallucinations.

S5Which message role holds the question a customer typed?

  • ASystem
  • BAssistant
  • CUser
  • DDeveloper
Show the answer

Answer: C. The user role holds the question or task for the current turn.

S6Why does a chat application send earlier messages with each new request?

  • ATo lower the cost of every request
  • BTo change the model between turns
  • CThe model has no memory between calls
  • DTo hide the system message from the user
Show the answer

Answer: C. Each call is independent, so earlier messages must be included.

6.2 Recall questions

R1Name the three message roles.

Show the answer

System, user and assistant.

R2What is the system prompt for?

Show the answer

Setting the assistant's role, rules, tone and limits.

R3What is few-shot prompting?

Show the answer

Giving a few examples of input and output in the prompt.

R4What does grounding a prompt mean?

Show the answer

Providing trusted source text so the answer comes from it.

R5What is prompt injection?

Show the answer

A user prompt that tries to override the developer's rules.

R6Why keep prompts focused?

Show the answer

Tokens cost money and fill the context window.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Roles system (developer rules), user (the question), assistant (the reply)
System prompt role, scope, tone, format, rules, examples
User prompt clear, specific, context, format, steps, length, source text
Shots zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot (examples as user and assistant messages)
No memory resend earlier messages; context window limit
Safety say "I don't know", ground answers, no secrets in prompts, beware prompt injection
